decision.note: GATE-01 binds one token to both KGA-D04 and KGA-D09. This record consumes only the KGA-D04 share: the seven KGA-G05 candidate owner identities are rejected. The thirteen per-ghost dispositions in the KGA-D09 ledger stay pending and are not applied here.

gapBinding.note: Rejecting the seven candidate identities removes the create-a-new-module option; it does not resolve which existing owner, if any, holds these directives. KGA-G05 stays a P0 open gap.

immutableRefs.note: Approval intake, EPOCH-03 chain, registry, gap inventory and the KGA-D09 ghost ledger are read by digest only; application state lives in the application-state ledger.

ledgerBoundary.note: The thirteen-row ghost ledger supplies the real ghost id and directive ref behind each rejected candidate. It stays byte-identical, candidate-unselected and pending: none of its thirteen per-ghost create/alias/fold/reject dispositions is decided or applied by this record.

invariants: The approved disposition is a rejection: all seven KGA-G05 candidate owner identities are refused and no node is created, no module is renamed and no parent or edge is written.
Rejection is not owner assignment: every ownerAssignment stays null, so no existing module gains these directives here.
Recording the rejection is a governance record, not gap closure: KGA-G05 stays a P0 open gap, its ownership resolution stays human-WBS-owner-decision and gapClosed stays false.
The GATE-01 token D04_D09=REJECT_13_GHOSTS is shared with KGA-D09; this record consumes only the candidate-owner-identity-rejection share of it.
The thirteen-row ghost ledger under KGA-D09 stays read-only evidence: byte-identical, candidate-unselected, pending, appliedByThisRecord=false, and its per-ghost dispositions stay open.
Each rejected row binds the real source ghost id and the existing directive that raised the claim; the six remaining ghost ids proposed no candidate owner and belong to KGA-D09 alone.
The registry keeps all ten decisions pending and unselected; the closure intake and EPOCH-03 chain are read by digest only.
No planning artifact here is runtime implementation evidence, a code-start permit or a readiness claim.
nonGoals: do not create, alias, fold, rename or re-parent any node for the seven candidate identities or the thirteen ghost ids
do not assign, infer or default an owner module for any rejected directive, and do not close KGA-G05
do not apply, select, reshape or re-hash the KGA-D09 ghost WBS binding ledger, and do not promote its pending rows
do not change the base queue, any registry decision, the closure intake or the EPOCH-03 authority chain
do not write runtime, platform or kernel product code, and do not treat this record as readiness or code-start evidence

rollback.trigger: a candidate identity gains a node or an owner, the rejected candidate set or its ghost/directive bindings drift, the KGA-D09 ledger is applied or its bytes change, the record scope widens beyond candidate-owner-identity rejection, or a fail-closed gate flag flips
rollback.action: revert this disposition record, its application-state row, the attestation contract, tests, pack sections and gate wiring as one shard
